questions.title: What is the difference between localStorage and sessionStorage?
questions.answer: localStorage persists data across browser sessions until it is removed. sessionStorage stores data for a particular origin and browser tab session. Both expose synchronous key-value APIs and store strings.
questions.underTheHood: The browser maintains storage areas associated with origins. sessionStorage is additionally partitioned by top-level browsing context.
pitfalls: Storage values are strings.
Web Storage APIs are synchronous.
Sensitive credentials should not be placed in Web Storage.
followUps: How do cookies differ from localStorage?

questions.title: What are cookies?
questions.answer: Cookies are small pieces of data associated with websites. They are commonly used for sessions and preferences and can be automatically included in HTTP requests according to their attributes.
questions.underTheHood: Browsers store cookies with attributes controlling scope, expiration and transmission. Attributes such as Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite affect security and request behavior.
pitfalls: HttpOnly cookies cannot be read through document.cookie.
Cookies can be included in network requests.
Cookie security depends on appropriate attributes.
followUps: What is the difference between cookies and localStorage?

questions.title: How does the Fetch API work?
questions.answer: The Fetch API provides a Promise-based interface for making HTTP requests. fetch() returns a Promise that fulfills with a Response object when a response becomes available.
questions.underTheHood: The browser performs the network operation and resolves or rejects the associated Promise according to the Fetch API's rules.
pitfalls: HTTP error statuses do not automatically reject fetch().
Response bodies are streams and are generally consumed once.
Network errors and HTTP errors must be distinguished.
followUps: What is the difference between fetch and XMLHttpRequest?

questions.title: What is AbortController?
questions.answer: AbortController provides a way to signal cancellation to APIs that support AbortSignal, including fetch().
questions.underTheHood: An AbortController owns a signal. Calling abort() marks the signal as aborted and notifies operations observing it.
pitfalls: AbortController only affects operations that support its signal.
Aborting a request does not guarantee that the server stopped processing it.
Abort errors should be distinguished from other failures.
followUps: How do you cancel a fetch request?
How can AbortController prevent stale requests?

questions.title: What are Web Workers?
questions.answer: Web Workers allow JavaScript to execute in background threads separate from the main browser thread. They are useful for computationally expensive work that would otherwise affect UI responsiveness.
questions.underTheHood: Workers have their own execution environment and communicate with other contexts through messages. Dedicated workers cannot directly manipulate the document DOM.
pitfalls: Workers cannot directly access the DOM.
Messages generally use structured cloning or transferable objects.
Workers introduce communication overhead.

questions.title: How does the browser render a web page?
questions.answer: Browsers parse HTML and CSS, construct the relevant document and style structures, calculate layout, paint visual content and composite the resulting layers for display.
questions.underTheHood: Rendering work depends on document structure, computed styles and layout requirements. Browsers may optimize or skip some stages for particular changes.
pitfalls: Not every style change triggers layout.
Repeated layout reads and writes can cause layout thrashing.
Long JavaScript tasks can delay rendering.

questions.title: What is requestAnimationFrame()?
questions.answer: requestAnimationFrame() schedules a callback before an upcoming browser repaint. It is commonly used for visual animations.
questions.underTheHood: The browser invokes animation-frame callbacks as part of its rendering update process when appropriate.
pitfalls: Animation frame timing depends on the display and browser scheduling.
Use timestamps for frame-rate-independent animations.
Callbacks may be paused in background tabs.
